solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cuddle bimbo somewhat without clothing?

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the phrase shows only the run of letters inside

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words once the outer ones are stripped away

explanation.surface: Someone hugs a scantily dressed young woman, perhaps with no clothes at all.
explanation.walkthrough: IMBOSOM sits inside bIMBO SOMewhat; only the first and last few letters are shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbosom is to clasp to one's breast, an old verb for hugging or embracing.

clue.text: Poet's featured in picture, strangely parrot-hued

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A poet appears in a painting whose colours are oddly like a parrot's plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks a Spenserian spelling: POURTRAHED is Spenser's form of portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Portrayed means depicted in a picture, and Spenser's archaic spelling of that past participle is this word.

clue.text: Bomb work mounting: it's armed at sea

indicators.note: in a down clue, something mounting climbs upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine
op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal job at sea involves a weapon that is primed and armed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pogge is the armed bullhead, a small spiny-plated sea fish, so 'armed' is literal armour here.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogge is a marine fish covered in bony plates, hence a creature that is armoured in the sea.

clue.text: Weedy group, half crazy to get stuck into beer

indicators.note: taking half a word keeps only its front portion and drops the rest
something stuck into another thing ends up lodged inside it

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
gaga means crazy or senile

explanation.surface: Someone half mad tucks into a pint with a scrawny gang of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weedy' looks like an insult for the group; it is literal, since seaweeds belong to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Algae are a group of simple plants including seaweeds, so a weedy group is a playful botanical description.

clue.text: Stodgy pudding producing club chat

blocks.note: a stick is a club or cudgel
to jaw is to talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A heavy pudding sparks conversation at a members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: Stickjaw is a slang name for a toffee or pudding so glutinous it glues the jaws together.

clue.text: Lewd display? I buzz off following earlier probe

blocks.note: a tent is a surgical probe or plug for a wound
taken as written
buzz off means go away

explanation.surface: Someone flees an indecent show after an inquiry starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The probe comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue; 'following earlier' sets that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentigo is an old medical term for morbid lustfulness or priapism, so a lewd display is a fair hinted gloss.

clue.text: Clam mostly heated in wooden bowl for Sandy

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped
one part placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: cog is a Scots word for a wooden bowl; Sandy is a stock Scotsman
heated means hot

explanation.surface: A clam is warmed in a wooden bowl for a Scotsman's supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy is the stock crossword Scotsman, so 'for Sandy' asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohog is a variant spelling of quahog, the edible hard-shelled clam of the American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Lamb's fur, reverse of dark – it lost value

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards
the letters i and t are lost from the following word

blocks.note: mirk is a variant of murk, darkness
merit means worth or value

explanation.surface: Lamb's fur fell in value as fashions turned against dark colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It lost value' tells you to take IT away from MERIT, leaving MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Krimmer is the grey curly fleece of young Crimean lambs, used as a fur.

clue.text: What'll make Jack pack fine porcelain

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
the instruction J as P is what turns one word into the other
the letter that replaces J in jack to make pack

explanation.surface: Something will make a lad called Jack pack away the good china.
explanation.walkthrough: Change J to P and jack becomes pack: the instruction 'J as P' spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasp is an old form of jasper, and jasper ware is Wedgwood's fine stoneware porcelain.

clue.text: One of Macbeth's witches described climbing round centre of pit

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
going round something encloses it
in a down clue, climbing reads upward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: drew means sketched or described
the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A witch from the Scottish play is pictured clambering out of a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The weird sisters are Macbeth's witches, and a weird alone can mean one of the Fates.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and Shakespeare a weird is a Fate or witch, as in the weird sisters who prophesy to Macbeth.

clue.text: Beef or duck served in wild onion

indicators.note: something served in a dish is placed inside it

blocks.note: moly is a wild garlic or onion
a duck is a score of nought, written O

explanation.surface: A menu offers beef or duck cooked with wild onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like a dish on the menu; here it means cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooly is a hornless cow, and beef can mean a bullock or cow raised for meat.

clue.text: Salad herb yielding distinctive smell on heat?

blocks.note: BO, body odour, is a distinctive personal smell
heat as in the heat of anger

explanation.surface: A salad herb gives off a strong scent when warmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered herb whose young leaves and flowers are added to salads and drinks.

clue.text: Nasty spirit but mostly whipped up with an egg

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word is kept, its last letter dropped
whipping up a mixture beats the ingredients into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty character is mostly cooked up from just an egg, like a soufflé.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T of but, then rearrange BU with AN and EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: A buggane is a malevolent goblin or ogre in Manx folklore, so a nasty spirit.

clue.text: Nice pillar fashioned sloping downwards all round

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped anew, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A handsome column is carved so that its surfaces slope down on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective, or the French city; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Periclinal is a geological term for strata dipping away on all sides from a central point, like a dome.

clue.text: Sign of fatigue for Scots on board brigantine

indicators.note: something on board a vessel is carried inside it

blocks.note: four letters carried inside this word

explanation.surface: A tired Scottish sailor shows signs of weariness aboard a two-masted ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Gant is Scots for a yawn, the classic outward sign that someone is tired.

clue.text: Traveller going to and fro in playsuit?

indicators.note: going to and then fro, the second reading runs back the other way

blocks.note: a Rom is a Romany, a Traveller
read a second time: a rep is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A Traveller children's garment is worn while running about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller' does double duty: the Romany going forward, then the sales rep coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rompers are a one-piece garment for small children at play, so a playsuit; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Packing e.g. vest in tight?

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter, points ignored

explanation.surface: Someone packing a suitcase crams a vest into a tight space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' seems to describe the squeeze; it means drunk, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To steeve is to stow or pack cargo tightly in a ship's hold, so steeving is packing.

clue.text: Drink knocked back, old poet's addled

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the word is turned backwards too

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A poet of old downed a drink and became befuddled.
explanation.walkthrough: Mard is Spenser's form of marred, which 'old poet's' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Marred means spoiled or damaged, close to addled in the sense of ruined, as an archaic Spenserian spelling.

clue.text: Regarding determinate variation, see wild riot etc imbibing strong drink

indicators.note: running wild means out of order, so these letters scatter
imbibing means taking in, so one part is swallowed inside the other

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
hogen is an old word for strong liquor, from hogen-mogen

explanation.surface: A rowdy disturbance breaks out after heavy drinking, recorded under some scientific heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split around HOGEN, an obscure word for strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthogenesis is evolution proceeding along a predetermined line, so orthogenetic concerns variation that is directed rather than random.

clue.text: Bad actor circling beach in precious antique?

indicators.note: circling something means surrounding it on all sides

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer
a lido is a bathing beach or open-air pool

explanation.surface: A poor actor strolls the seafront clutching a valuable old object.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a sacred relic is precious and ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: A halidom is an archaic word for a holy relic or sacred object, something old and treasured.

clue.text: Ruin part in best repertory

indicators.note: part in means a portion found within the following words

blocks.note: seven letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An actor's role in a top repertory company threatens to wreck the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrepe is a legal term meaning to lay waste or commit waste on land, hence to ruin or despoil.

clue.text: Skullcap

blocks.note: the only word printed: this is the competition word, so the setter gives a bare definition
competitors supply their own wordplay; the printed word is the meaning alone

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one answer is given only by its meaning; entrants write the clue themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A calotte is a small close-fitting cap worn on the crown, such as a priest's zucchetto.

clue.text: What rattles – look at price involved – varied shellfish

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside something else

blocks.note: a maraca is a gourd rattle shaken in Latin music
la is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
cost means price

explanation.surface: A rattling sound accompanies a look at what the mixed seafood costs.
explanation.walkthrough: La is an archaic exclamation meaning look or behold, seen mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Malacostraca is the large and diverse class of crustaceans that includes crabs, lobsters and shrimps.

clue.text: Vagrant person, parasite avoided by CID

indicators.note: the letters avoided are left out of the word

blocks.note: a chalcid is a tiny parasitic wasp
taken as written; the CID is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Police detectives steer clear of a homeless sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CID from the end of CHALCID.
explanation.definitionFit: Chal is a Romany word for a fellow or person, used in English for a vagabond.

clue.text: Peevish? Not what I am doffing topper

indicators.note: doffing a topper takes off the hat, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: this is a down clue, so it is not an across

explanation.surface: Someone irritable insists they are not who they seem, and takes off their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: a down clue is not an across one, and the A comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means irritable or annoyed, a direct synonym of peevish.

clue.text: Henry's included in derisive shout – it omits nothing

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout
H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry joins in the jeering, missing no chance to heckle.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchall is a container or term that takes in everything, so nothing is left out.

clue.text: Endless song about international capital

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off
about means going round, so one part is enclosed

blocks.note: a carol is a festive song
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A never-ending tune circulates around a cosmopolitan city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Flirt with poppet, full of sexiness (5, two words)

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment like poppet
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with a darling who oozes sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on someone is to make romantic advances, informal for flirting with them.

clue.text: Poll's associated with me? Poll led by adult maybe

blocks.note: A was the film certificate for adult audiences
both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A parrot talks about itself and its grown-up companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' suggests a parrot, but a poll is the head, and a pineapple wears a leafy crown on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Anana is an old name for the pineapple, a fruit topped by a tuft of leaves, a head or poll.

clue.text: Network's genuine, holding it back

indicators.note: back means running in the reverse direction
holding means keeping something inside

blocks.note: real means genuine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broadcasting network claims authenticity while holding back the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Retial means relating to a net or network, from Latin rete, so it is the adjective for network's.

clue.text: Trendy old twit

blocks.note: first meaning: fashionable or stylish, in US informal use
second meaning: an obsolete word for a simpleton or fool

explanation.surface: A fashionable old fool keeps up appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony means smart or high-toned informally, and also once meant a foolish person or ninny.

clue.text: I'll be caught by chance in bankruptcy

indicators.note: caught by means held inside something else

blocks.note: a run at something is a chance or try
the clue's I is the piece to insert

explanation.surface: A gambler says they will be ruined if luck takes them to bankruptcy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is financial collapse, the state of having lost everything, much like bankruptcy.

clue.text: Like creeping plants, forming odd pattern

indicators.note: something odd is irregular, so these letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Creeping plants spread out in an irregular design.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptant is a botanical and zoological term for creeping or crawling along the ground.

clue.text: Rankers in army abroad going for foreign lady

indicators.note: one part placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: sena is the Hindi word for an army
OR, other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers in an overseas army chase after a local woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, so a foreign lady.

clue.text: Primer, once new, held in spoon?

indicators.note: something held in another sits inside it

blocks.note: doat is a variant of dote, and to spoon is to dote lovingly
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new schoolbook is tucked inside a cutlery drawer, beside the spoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoon' is the old verb for behaving lovingly, not the cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A donat was an old grammar or elementary textbook, named after the Latin grammarian Donatus.

clue.text: Founder of democracy (John), first in Seychelles, getting agent's fee?

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
John Pym led the parliamentary opposition to Charles I
one is the first number

explanation.surface: A parliamentary pioneer heads first to the Seychelles, with a spy's payment in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: John Pym, the 17th-century parliamentarian, is hailed as a defender of parliamentary government.
explanation.definitionFit: Spy-money is money paid to a spy or secret agent for their services, an agent's fee.
